memory_update.text: NET is a high-attention reference anchor for election-website cybersecurity via Cloudflare's Athenian Project; useful benchmark, not the underfollowed alpha lane.
TLS is an underfollowed small-cap candidate for public-sector cyber/identity/GRC exposure, but direct election-agency evidence remains unverified.
IDN is a speculative micro-cap identity-verification candidate; direct election use must be verified before it survives later Serenity layers.
GAHC/GES is a speculative OTC micro-cap direct election-services trace, but asset-sale disclosures may remove or dilute the exposure.

Core US voting-system vendors such as major voting-machine, ballot-marking, and election-management-system providers appear mostly private; future passes should map private vendors to public suppliers, equipment, software, mail, cybersecurity, and certified component dependencies.

The more investable public chokepoints may sit one layer away from voting machines: DDoS/WAF/CDN, identity verification, cyber GRC, mail-ballot automation, printing/inserting/sorting equipment, secure hosting, and state/local procurement integrators.

summary: Expanded the election administration / election cybersecurity node through a scarce-supplier lens. Direct public-market exposure is limited because core voting-system vendors are often private, but plausible US-public candidates exist in adjacent chokepoints: election-website DDoS/WAF/CDN protection, public-sector cyber/identity compliance, authoritative ID verification workflows, and a highly speculative OTC direct election-services asset. No buy/sell view is implied.
